questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “ There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today’s world. ” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. ( You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay. )
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today’s world. As study, work and daily life move online, the ability to use digital tools wisely has become a basic survival skill rather than an optional advantage.

This importance is easy to feel in real situations. During the pandemic, all my courses were shifted to online platforms, and only classmates who could navigate video meetings, submit assignments and search for reliable sources kept up with the pace. Those who struggled with the technology quickly fell behind, not because they were less clever, but because they lacked the digital skills the new setting demanded. The same gap appears in the job market, where employers now expect graduates to handle data, communicate online and tell trustworthy information from rumours.

Therefore, digital literacy is no longer a bonus but a necessity. By actively learning to process information, protect our online safety and keep updating our skills, we can turn technology into a real advantage instead of a barrier.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 本场次听力只有一份音频，本套听力与同场第一套同卷；原文、题目与答案取自该套真题。考场多套卷的选项顺序可能不同，这里沿用第一套的顺序。在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: W: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice.
transcript.zh: W: 谢谢你在这么短的时间内抽空见我，Stephen。

transcript.text: M: Not a problem, Margaret. Now, please give me some good news. Have you agreed to my last proposal?
transcript.zh: M: 没问题，Margaret。现在，请告诉我一些好消息。你同意我上次的提议了吗？

transcript.text: W: I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.
transcript.zh: W: 确实同意了。我希望签署协议，前提是对合同做一处小改动。

transcript.text: M: Margaret, we've been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations. Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients, or not? I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.
transcript.zh: M: Margaret，我们为这件事来回磋商、不断修改，已经快一年了。你到底确定要为你的客户达成一项赞助协议，还是不想？我之所以这样问，是因为坦率地说，我这边有些人已经快失去耐心了。

transcript.text: W: I understand your concerns. But as I'm sure you understand, we hold our clients' best interests to be of the utmost concern. We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts, rest assured, we all appreciate your firm's patience.
transcript.zh: W: 我理解你的担忧。不过，我相信你也明白，我们最关心的是客户的最大利益。因此，我们会仔细审阅所有合同的细节，请放心，我们都很感谢贵公司的耐心。

transcript.text: M: OK, fine. So what change do you wish to make?
transcript.zh: M: 好吧，没问题。那么你想做什么改动？

transcript.text: W: Essentially, we would like the new deal to exclude the Middle East. That's all.
transcript.zh: W: 基本上，我们希望新协议不包括中东地区。就这些。

transcript.text: M: The Middle East? Why?
transcript.zh: M: 中东地区？为什么？

transcript.text: W: My client has a couple of other prospective marketing deals from companies in the Middle East. Those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client's image in the Middle East only. Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
transcript.zh: W: 我的客户还收到几家中东公司的其他潜在营销合作邀约。如果这些邀约最终落实，对方将只在中东地区使用我客户的形象。因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们需要确保这两项营销活动在地域上不会重叠。

transcript.text: M: What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?
transcript.zh: M: 你说的中东业务具体属于哪个行业？

transcript.text: W: Real estate.
transcript.zh: W: 房地产。

transcript.text: M: Well, that should be okay then. So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest. Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people. I don't foresee any problem, though. The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.
transcript.zh: M: 那应该没问题。只要产品与我们的食品和饮料市场有很大不同，就不应存在利益冲突。不过，我还是得把这件事拿去和我的团队确认一下。但我预计不会有什么问题。中东对我们来说是个微不足道的市场，不过我仍然需要和几个部门核实一下。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she will do?

options.text: Reply to the man's last proposal within a short time.
Sign the agreement if one small change is made to it.
Make a sponsorship deal for her client at the meeting.
Give the man some good news regarding the contract.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：W: I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.信号：被问者的直接应答 + I wish to 表态 。上一句男方问 Have you agreed to my last proposal?，女方紧接着应答 I have, indeed. And I wish to s…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 借了男方话里的 my last proposal 拼成 Reply to the man's last proposal within a short time.，可她在 I have, indeed 里已经回复并表态要签，根本没说 "短时间内回复"，within a short time 是凭空加的。 借用原文：Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：C 的 Make a sponsorship deal for her client at the meeting. 用了录音里的 make a sponsorship deal for your clients，但那是男方反问 "你到底要不要做这笔交易"，并非女方此刻 "我要做什么" 的回答；本题问的是她当下表态，答案是签约。 借用原文：please give me some good news
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 的 Give the man some good news regarding the contract. 盗了男方那句 please give me some good news，那是男方的请求 / 期待，女方并没说 "我要给你好消息"，她说的是愿意签约。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I wish to sign the agreement ↔ Sign the agreement I wish to do = 表示要做该动作）

questions.evidenceText: W: I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.

questions.stem: What does the man say about some people he represents?

options.text: They are afraid time is running out.
They are used to making alterations.
They are concerned about the details.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：M: I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.信号：因果 because 后给出他对己方人员的真实描述 。他用 because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience，because 引出…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 的 time is running out 盗用了录音 running out of patience 里的 running out，却把宾语偷换成 time。录音里耗尽的是耐心，不是时间，B 在 running out 后面动了手脚。 借用原文：we've been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations
optionAnalysis.C: 答非所问：C 的 used to making alterations 取自录音 making alterations，但那是男方说双方 "这一年来回改来改去" 的背景，不是在描述 "我方那些人现在什么状态"，答非所问。 借用原文：We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：D 的 concerned about the details 实际对应女方后面说的 We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts，那是女方一边推敲细节，与男方所说 "我那边的人没耐心" 是两拨人、两回事。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（running out of patience ↔ becoming impatient running out of patience = impatient，同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: M: I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.

questions.stem: What reason does the woman give for the new deal to exclude the Middle East?

options.text: To tap the food and beverage market.
To avoid any conflict of interest.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：W: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.信号：in order to / therefore 双因果信号引出真目的 。她先讲客户在中东另有营销意向，再用 Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would ne…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 的 To prevent geographical discrimination. 蹭了录音 overlap geographically 里的 geographically，造出 "地域歧视"。原文讲的是两个营销活动地域别重叠，与 "歧视" 毫不相干，是借词造假。 借用原文：So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market
optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：B 的 To tap the food and beverage market. 用了录音 our food and beverage market，但那是男方在第12段说自家所属行业，与女方排除中东的理由无关；她的理由是避免冲突，不是去开发某市场。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 的 To reduce unfair competition. 听着像商务套话，但录音通篇没说要减少不公平竞争，她讲的是避免客户形象在同一地域撞车的利益冲突，competition 一词原文压根没出现。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（in order to avoid any conflict ↔ To avoid any conflict of interest. avoid any conflict 与选项几乎原义对应）

questions.evidenceText: W: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.

questions.stem: What does the man say about the Middle East?

options.text: It is a potential market for food and beverage.
It is very attractive for real estate developers.
It is a negligible market for his company.
It is very different from other markets.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P12）：M: The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.信号：他对中东的直接评价句 + 形容词 negligible 。他直说 The Middle East is a negligible market for us，主系表结构直接给出评价形容词 negligible，是对中…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：A 的 It is a potential market for food and beverage. 把中东说成 "有潜力"，与他原话 a negligible market（可忽略）正好相反；food and beverage 又是蹭了他讲己方行业的熟词，双重误导。 借用原文：Real estate
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：B 的 It is very attractive for real estate developers. 借了女方说的中东 Real estate，但那是女方客户在中东另有房地产营销意向，并非男方对中东市场的评价，张冠李戴。 借用原文：So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：D 的 It is very different from other markets. 盗用了 the product is very different from our food and beverage market 里的 very different，但原文说的是 "产品" 与食饮市场不同，不是说 "中东市场" 与别的市场不同，主语被偷换。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a negligible market for us ↔ a negligible market for his company for us = for his company，几乎原义）

questions.evidenceText: M: The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.

transcript.text: M: Next, we have a special science-related news story. Paula Hancocks at the Denver Observatory. Paula, what is the big story over there?
transcript.zh: M：接下来是一则特别的科学新闻报道。丹佛天文台的 Paula Hancocks，Paula，那边有什么重大新闻？

transcript.text: W: Hi, John. Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited. In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky.
transcript.zh: W：你好，John。是的，这里的所有天文学家都非常兴奋。事实上，整个北美以及北半球其他地区的太空爱好者今晚都会聚集到山顶，观看夜空。

transcript.text: M: Why? What's the big event? Is there an eclipse happening soon?
transcript.zh: M：为什么？有什么重大事件？很快要发生日食了吗？

transcript.text: W: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years. For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
transcript.zh: W：今晚，地球将与 Oppenheimer 彗星近距离接近。这是100多年来我们的星球距离此类现象最近的一次。因此，预计今晚会有数千人仰望天空，观看这个令人震撼的天体。

transcript.text: M: How far away is this comet? Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
transcript.zh: M：这颗彗星距离我们有多远？人们用肉眼能看到它吗？

transcript.text: W: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy. But nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope. People will only see a blur without one. However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment. Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
transcript.zh: W：Oppenheimer 彗星仍会位于数百万英里之外，在我们银河系的边缘。不过，这仍然算是相对较近的距离，近到人们可以通过望远镜清楚地观测它。没有望远镜的话，人们只能看到一团模糊的影像。不过，这并不意味着必须使用专业设备。即使是最普通的望远镜，也足以让人们观测并惊叹于这个飞行中的天体。

transcript.text: M: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event. Where will this comet be in the sky? How can people find it?
transcript.zh: M：我们的许多观众都会想知道，他们怎样才能参与这场一生难遇的活动。这颗彗星会出现在天空的什么位置？人们该如何找到它？

transcript.text: W: The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator. However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky. And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.
transcript.zh: W：这颗彗星几乎正好位于正北方，在赤道上方60度的位置。不过，找到这颗彗星确实非常困难。这里的科学家告诉我，有很多手机应用可以帮助大家定位。

transcript.text: M: How fantastic! Thank you, Paula, for the information.
transcript.zh: M：太棒了！Paula，感谢你提供这些信息。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about all the astronomers at the Denver Observatory?

options.text: They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon.
They are celebrating a big event on mountain tops.
They are enthusiastic about big science-related stories.
They are joined by astronomers all across North America.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited.信号：被问者的直接应答 。男士在 what is the big story over there? 抛出问题，女士开口第一句 all the astronomers on site here are very excit…

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：录音 congregating on mountain tops 确实念到"山顶"，但那是"聚集去观星"，不是 celebrating a big event on mountain tops 的"在山顶庆祝"，且主语是北美各地爱好者，非天文台的天文学家。 借用原文：a special science-related news story
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：开头 a special science-related news story 念到"科学相关"，C 项 enthusiastic about big science-related stories 直接搬这串词，但录音说的是天文学家"为这次天象兴奋"，不是"热衷各种科学新闻故事"，把对一次具体天象的兴奋偷换成对科学故事的泛泛热衷。 借用原文：space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：录音 space enthusiasts all across North America 说的是"北美各地的爱好者要聚集"，D 项 joined by astronomers all across North America 把它改成"天文台的天文学家被北美各地天文学家加入"，主语和事件都被偷换，原文没有这层意思。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（all the astronomers on site here are very excited ↔ They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon. excited 同义改写为 thrilled）

questions.evidenceText: Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about the Oppenheimer comet?

options.text: It will be the most formidable of its kind in over a century.
It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years.
It will eclipse many other such events in human history.
It will be seen most clearly from Denver's mountain tops.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.信号：正面定性句 + 时间数字 。女士直接给彗星定性 It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years，"closes…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音后文 this formidable object 确有 "formidable"，A 项 the most formidable of its kind in over a century 便把"百年"嫁接到"最厉害"上；但原文里"百年"修饰的是"距离最近"，从没说它是百年来"最厉害"的，是把数字按到了错的形容词上。 借用原文：Is there an eclipse happening soon?
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：eclipse many other such events in human history 借"eclipse"（此处作动词"使相形见绌"）和前文 Is there an eclipse happening soon? 的"日食"玩文字游戏，原文从没说这颗彗星"使人类历史上其他天象相形见绌"，属凭空拔高。 借用原文：congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：seen most clearly from Denver's mountain tops 把前文 the Denver Observatory 的"丹佛"和 mountain tops 的"山顶"拼到一起，但原文只说爱好者会聚到山顶观星，从没说"从丹佛的山顶看得最清楚"，是把零散原词攒成一句没说过的话。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years ↔ It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years. 主被动对调 + 数字同义）

questions.evidenceText: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.

questions.stem: What does the woman say people will only see in the sky without a telescope?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：People will only see a blur without one.信号：条件 without one + only 直陈 。这句用 without one（one 指代上文 telescope）锁定"不用望远镜"的前提，再用 only see a blur 直说看到什么，前提和结果都摆明…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：录音通篇没说不用望远镜会看到"星星"，Stars. 是凭"看星空"的常识脑补出来的，原文只说看到"一团模糊"。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：on the edge of our galaxy 念到"星系边缘"，但那是说彗星"所在的位置"，不是"不用望远镜看到的东西"，C 项 The edge of our galaxy. 把"它在哪"偷换成"看到什么"。 借用原文：Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：wonder at this flying object 念到 "flying object"，但那是"用普通望远镜能观赏到的彗星"，D 项 An ordinary flying object. 把它挪到"不用望远镜"的前提下——条件正好反了，不用望远镜只见模糊团，看不清是个"飞行物"。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（People will only see a blur without one ↔ blur. 原句直取，前提一致）

questions.evidenceText: People will only see a blur without one.

questions.stem: What do scientists at the Denver Observatory advise amateurs do to facilitate their observation?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P8）：And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.信号：建议句 + 与题干同词 facilitate 。女士转述科学家的建议 there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this，"scientists…told…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：录音 that does not mean one needs professional equipment 明确说"并不需要专业设备"，A 项 Use professional equipment. 直接搬这串原词却把否定改成肯定，意思正好反了。 借用原文：will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音 congregating on mountain tops 念到"山顶"，B 项 Climb to the nearby heights.（爬到附近高处）借此设套，但那是说爱好者去哪儿聚集，不是科学家"为方便观测给的建议"，问的根本不是同一件事。 借用原文：The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音 The comet will be almost exactly due north 念到"正北"，那是在说彗星"在天上的位置"，C 项 Fix their eyes due north. 把"它在正北方"偷换成"建议人们眼睛盯着正北"，而科学家给的方便观测的办法是用 app，不是"盯着北方"。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this ↔ Make use of phone apps. 存在句 → 祈使建议）

questions.evidenceText: And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.

transcript.text: Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world. While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?
transcript.zh: 膳食指南构成了世界各地营养建议和相关法规的基础。尽管现有大多数指南背后都有强有力的科学共识，但最近有一个问题引发了争议：是否应当提醒消费者避免食用超加工食品？

transcript.text: Two papers published today in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra-processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems. The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of São Paulo and Arne Astrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation, will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate August 14th during NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE.
transcript.zh: 今天发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的两篇论文，分别阐述了支持和反对使用“超加工食品”这一概念的理由，以帮助在传统食品分类体系之外进一步制定膳食指南。论文作者、圣保罗大学的Carlos Monteiro和Novo Nordisk Foundation的Arne Astrup，将于8月14日在NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE期间举行的线上直播辩论中讨论这一问题。

transcript.text: The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed. The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product. Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient; examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready-to-heat products, and reconstituted meat products.
transcript.zh: 这场辩论围绕Monteiro及其同事制定的一套体系展开，该体系根据食品的工业加工程度对其进行分类，范围从未加工食品到超加工食品。该体系将超加工食品定义为：通过一系列加工步骤制成的食品，在这些步骤中，先从食品中提取物质，再使用化学品对其进行改变，以配制出最终产品。超加工食品通常被设计成价格低廉、美味可口且方便食用；其中包括软饮料和糖果、包装零食和糕点、即热食品以及再制肉制品等。

transcript.text: Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods—which are packed high in salt, sugar, and fat—with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet. While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra-processed foods in dietary recommendations and government policies.
transcript.zh: 研究表明，食用超加工食品会导致体重增加并提高患慢性疾病的风险；这类食品含有大量盐、糖和脂肪，即使在对膳食中盐、糖和脂肪的含量进行调整后，这些关联仍然存在。尽管这些关联背后的机制尚未被完全理解，Monteiro认为，现有证据已经足以支持在膳食建议和政府政策中劝阻人们食用超加工食品。

questions.stem: What question is said to have recently stirred debate?

options.text: Whether consumers should be warned against ultra-processed foods.
Whether there is sufficient scientific consensus on dietary guidelines.
Whether guidelines can form the basis for nutrition advice to consumers.
Whether food scientists will agree on the concept of ultra-processed foods.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?信号：冒号后正面点出争论问题 。信号是 one question has recently stirred debate: 这一句——它直接照应题干 stirred debate，而冒号之后的 should consume…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B Whether there is sufficient scientific consensus on dietary guidelines. 借用了录音里 strong scientific consensus 这个原词，但原文说的是「围绕大多数指南已存在强共识」，共识是既定背景、不是争论的问题；真正起争论的是冒号后那句，B 答非所问。 借用原文：Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world.
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C Whether guidelines can form the basis for nutrition advice to consumers. 几乎照搬开篇 Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice，但原文这句是肯定的陈述（指南本就是营养建议的基础），并非被拿来争论的疑问，C 把陈述句伪装成争论点。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D Whether food scientists will agree on the concept of ultra-processed foods. 用了话题词 ultra-processed foods，但「食品科学家是否会就这一概念达成一致」原文根本没说——录音争论的是「要不要警告消费者」，不是「科学家认不认这个概念」，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods? ↔ Whether consumers should be warned against ultra-processed foods. 疑问句→Whether名词从句，warned against=warned to avoid）

questions.stem: How does the system developed by Monteiro and colleagues classify foods?

options.text: By the labor cost for the final products.
By the degree of industrial processing.
By the extent of chemical alteration.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed.信号：专名+classifies…by 直接给出分类标准 。信号是题干专名 Monteiro 在录音里复现，紧跟的 classifies foods by their degree of industrial proces…

optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C By the extent of chemical alteration. 来自后一句 alter them with chemicals——但那句是在「定义什么叫超加工食品」，分类的标准是「工业加工程度」，化学改变只是超加工这一端的特征描述，不是整套系统的分类轴，C 答非所问。 借用原文：beyond conventional food classification systems
optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A By the labor cost for the final products. 里 final products 蹭了原文 formulate the final product 的字眼，但「按人工成本分类」录音从没说过；原文提到的是 cheap（便宜），与「人工成本」不是一回事，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：D By the convention of classification. 借了 food classification 里的 classification 一词，但原文恰恰强调这套系统是「超越」传统分类的——第2段说要 beyond conventional food classification systems，方向正好相反，D 取了被否定的那一端。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（by their degree of industrial processing ↔ By the degree of industrial processing. 近乎原话对应，仅去掉物主代词）

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods—which are packed high in salt, sugar, and fat—with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet.信号：Studies have linked…with 正面给出关联后果 。信号是 Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods…with weight …

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A Increased consumers' expenses. 蹭了第3段超加工食品 designed to be cheap 的语境联想，但原文说这类食品「便宜」，恰恰不是「让消费者花费增加」；研究关联的是健康后果，不是花钱，A 属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C People's misunderstanding of nutrition. 借了全文反复出现的 nutrition 话题词，但「人们对营养的误解」录音从没说过；研究关联的是体重和疾病，不是认知误解，C 无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D Children's dislike for unprocessed foods. 用了第3段 unprocessed 一词，但「孩子不喜欢未加工食品」录音完全没提，且把话题从「健康后果」偷换成「儿童口味偏好」，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（an increased risk of chronic diseases ↔ Greater risk of chronic diseases. increased=greater，risk of chronic diseases 同义保留）

transcript.text: Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints. According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently. With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully. When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
transcript.zh: 信不信由你，限制有益于人类的创造力。心理学家认为，当你可利用的资源较少时，你实际上会开始以不同的方式看待世界。有了限制，你会将 mental energy 投入到更具资源性地采取行动上。面对挑战时，你会想出新的方法，让自己做得更好。

transcript.text: The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher. People who invent new products are not limited by what they don't have or can't do. They leverage their limitations to push themselves even further. Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use. They created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
transcript.zh: 最成功的创意人士知道，限制会促使他们的思维跃得更高。发明新产品的人不会受到自己没有什么或不能做什么的限制。他们利用自身的局限，推动自己更进一步。许多产品和服务之所以诞生，是因为创始人发现自己所使用的产品或服务存在局限。他们根据当时对自己不起作用的地方创造了创新。

transcript.text: Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation. In a 2015 study which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways. When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to. Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes. Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
transcript.zh: 创新是创意人士对局限的回应。在一项于2015年开展的研究中，伊利诺伊大学的Ravi Mehta和约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的Meng Zhu考察了对稀缺或富足的思考如何影响人们创造性地使用资源，并发现人们根本没有动力以新颖的方式利用手头的资源。当人们面临资源稀缺时，他们会迫使自己以不那么传统的方式使用资源，因为他们不得不这样做。障碍可以拓宽你的认知，并开启你的思维过程。持续存在的限制有助于你提高将不相关的想法和概念联系起来的能力。

transcript.text: Marissa Mayer, former vice president for search products and user experience at Google, once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg, "Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome; Creativity thrives best when constrained."
transcript.zh: 谷歌前搜索产品和用户体验副总裁Marissa Mayer曾在彭博社的一篇刊物中写道：“限制能够塑造问题、聚焦问题，并提供有待克服的明确挑战；创造力在受到限制时最能蓬勃发展。”

questions.stem: What do psychologists say people do when they are short of resources?

options.text: They begin to think of the benefits of constraints.
They try to seek solutions from creative people.
They try hard to maximize their mental energy.
They begin to see the world in a different way.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently.信号：题干信号词 psychologists 顺听定位 。题干问的是 psychologists（心理学家）的说法，录音里恰有 According to psychologists 这一引述信号，紧跟其后的 you act…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 用了全文话题词 constraints，但 think of the benefits of constraints（想到约束的好处）是录音从未说过的动作，录音说的是人开始换个方式看世界，A 只是借 constraints 这个耳熟的词诱你误选。 借用原文：you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 说人去 seek solutions from creative people（向有创造力的人求解），录音通篇讲的是人自己换方式看世界、自己更灵活地用资源，从没说去向别人求助，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 出现 maximize their mental energy，录音确有 dedicate your mental energy（投入心智能量）这个词，但原文说的是把心智能量投入到更灵活地行动，不是 maximize（最大化）能量本身，C 盗用 mental energy 这个原词却篡改了它的动作。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（begin to see the world differently ↔ begin to see the world in a different way 副词换介词短语）

questions.stem: What does the passage say about innovation?

options.text: It is characteristic of all creative people.
It is essential to pushing society forward.
It is a creative person's response to limitation.
It is an impetus to socio-economic development.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation.信号：段首定性句直接定义 。第三段开头 Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation. 是一句标准的 X is Y 定性句，主语正是题干的 innovat…

optionAnalysis.A: 偷换概念：A 说创新 characteristic of all creative people（所有有创造力的人的特征），录音说的是创新是有创造力者对限制的回应，并没有断言它是所有这类人都具备的特征，all 把范围说死，属偷换概念。 借用原文：constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher
optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：B 说创新 essential to pushing society forward（对推动社会前进至关重要），录音有 impetus（推动力）一词，但说的是约束给人的头脑以跃升的推动力，并非创新对推动社会前进必不可少，B 把对象偷偷拔高到社会层面，过度推断。 借用原文：constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说创新是 impetus to socio-economic development（社会经济发展的推动力），impetus 虽是原词，但 socio-economic development（社会经济发展）录音从头到尾没提，纯属拿原词拼接出一个原文没有的结论。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a creative person's response to limitation ↔ a creative person's response to limitation 罕见的近乎原句对应）

questions.stem: What did a 2015 study by Ravi Mehta and Meng Zhu find?

options.text: Scarcity or abundance of resources has little impact on people's creativity.
Innovative people are not constrained in connecting unrelated concepts.
People have no incentive to use available resources in new ways.
Creative people tend to consume more available resources.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways.信号：人名加 found that 引出发现 。录音里 Ravi Mehta 与 Meng Zhu 两个人名后紧跟 found that，这是研究发现的标志信号，that 引导的从句就是答案内容；听到人名加 found t…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：A 说 Scarcity or abundance of resources has little impact on people's creativity（资源稀缺或充裕对创造力影响不大），录音确实研究了 scarcity or abundance 如何影响创造性用资源，但结论恰恰是影响很大、稀缺反而激发创造，A 把研究的对象词盗来却得出与原文相反的结论。 借用原文：Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：B 说 Innovative people are not constrained in connecting unrelated concepts（创新者在联结不相关概念时不受约束），录音末句确有 connecting unrelated ideas and concepts 这个搭配，但那是说持续的约束帮助人更善于联结不相关概念，并非这项 2015 研究的发现，B 把别处的原词搬到研究结论上，答非所问。 借用原文：use what's available to them in novel ways
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说 Creative people tend to consume more available resources（有创造力的人倾向消耗更多现有资源），available resources 蹭了原文的词，但 consume more（消耗更多）录音从未提及，录音讲的是以新方式使用资源，不是消耗更多，纯属编造。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways ↔ no incentive to use available resources in new ways 近义词逐处替换）

options.text: It is key to a company's survival.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome; Creativity thrives best when constrained.信号：题干限定词 creativity 锁后半句 。Mayer 的引述有前后两句，前半 Constraints shape and focus problems 主语是约束，后半 Creativity thrives be…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A 说创造力 key to a company's survival（对公司生存至关重要），虽然录音提到 Mayer 曾是 Google 的副总裁，但她写的话里根本没提公司生存，A 凭 Google 这一职务背景臆造出公司话题，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：B 说 It shapes and focuses problems.，这句确实摘自 Mayer 的话 Constraints shape and focus problems，但原文该动作的主语是 Constraints（约束）不是 creativity，题干问的是关于 creativity 的内容，B 把约束做的事安到了创造力头上，主语张冠李戴。 借用原文：provide clear challenges to overcome
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 说创造力 essential to meeting challenges（对应对挑战至关重要），录音里 challenges 一词出自 provide clear challenges to overcome，说的是约束提供需克服的挑战，而非创造力对应对挑战必不可少，C 盗用 challenges 偷换了逻辑关系。

transcript.text: Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts. These strategies are learned in childhood. Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations. We just do whatever seems to come naturally. But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts. When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person. How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict. Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified.
transcript.zh: 不同的人会采用不同的冲突处理策略。这些策略是在童年时期学会的。通常，我们并没有意识到自己在冲突情境中是如何行动的，只是按照看似自然而然的方式去做。但我们确实都有自己的策略，而且由于这种策略是后天习得的，所以我们始终可以通过学习新的、更有效的冲突处理方式来改变它。当你卷入冲突时，有两个主要方面需要考虑：实现个人目标，以及与对方保持良好关系。个人目标对你的重要程度，以及这段关系对你的重要程度，都会影响你在冲突中的行为。根据这两个方面，可以确定五种冲突处理风格。

transcript.text: The turtle. Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts. They give up their personal goals and relationships. They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
transcript.zh: 龟型。乌龟会缩进壳里以避免冲突。它们放弃个人目标和人际关系。它们认为，与其面对冲突，不如退出冲突更容易。

transcript.text: The shark. Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict. They seek to achieve their goals at all costs. Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing. Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement. Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy, and failure.
transcript.zh: 鲨鱼型。鲨鱼试图迫使对方接受自己提出的冲突解决方案，从而压倒对方。它们不惜一切代价追求实现自己的目标。鲨鱼认为，冲突的解决方式是一方获胜、另一方失败。获胜会让鲨鱼产生自豪感和成就感；失败则会让它们感到软弱、无能和挫败。

transcript.text: The teddy bear. Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people. They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships. They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
transcript.zh: 泰迪熊型。泰迪熊希望得到他人的接纳和喜爱。它们认为，为了保持和谐，应当避免冲突，并相信讨论冲突会损害人际关系。它们放弃自己的目标，以维护这段关系。

transcript.text: The fox. Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people. They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals. They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
transcript.zh: 狐狸型。狐狸对自身目标以及与他人的关系都抱有适度的关注。它们放弃一部分自己的目标，并说服冲突中的对方也放弃一部分目标。它们寻求一种能让双方都获得一些利益的冲突解决方案。

transcript.text: The owl. Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved. They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people. They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem. By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship. Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.
transcript.zh: 猫头鹰型。猫头鹰把冲突视为需要解决的问题。它们认为，冲突能够通过减少两个人之间的紧张关系来改善人际关系。它们试图展开讨论，将冲突界定为一个问题。通过寻求既能满足自己又能满足对方的解决方案，猫头鹰得以维持这段关系。在找到既能实现自己的目标、又能实现对方目标的解决方案之前，猫头鹰不会感到满意；在紧张情绪和负面感受得到彻底解决之前，它们也不会感到满意。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say strategies for managing conflicts can always be changed?

options.text: Because they have to be properly personalized.
Because there can be more effective strategies.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts.信号：because 直接交代原因 。这句里 because it is learned, we can always change it 是赤裸裸的因果结构："because + 原因"紧跟着"can always ch…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音确实说过 We just do whatever seems to come naturally，但那是讲"我们平时不自觉、顺其自然地行事"，并非"策略能被改变的原因"。B 把这个原词搬来当原因，恰恰用反了——天生自然反而是难改的那一面。 借用原文：a personal strategy

transcript.text: The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health. Scientists hope that cracking the genetic code of plants and animals could help uncover new treatments for infectious diseases, slow aging, improve crops in agriculture, and create new bio-materials.
transcript.zh: 地球上现存的全部150万种已知动植物的遗传密码将被测序，以帮助拯救濒临灭绝的物种并促进人类健康。科学家希望，破解动植物的遗传密码能够帮助发现传染病的新疗法、延缓衰老、改良农业作物，并创造新的生物材料。

transcript.text: In Britain, organizations including the Natural History Museum, the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew and the Wellcome Sanger Institute have joined forces to sequence Britain's 66,000 species of animals and plants. Dubbed the Darwin Tree of Life Project, it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million. Once completed, all the information will be publicly available to researchers.
transcript.zh: 在英国，包括自然历史博物馆、邱园皇家植物园和Wellcome Sanger研究所在内的多个组织已经联合起来，为英国的6.6万种动植物进行基因测序。该项目被称为“达尔文生命之树项目”，预计将耗时10年，耗资1亿英镑。项目完成后，所有信息都将向研究人员公开。

transcript.text: Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change, which has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500. It is the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago. Scientists say that sequencing every species will revolutionise the understanding of biology and evolution, bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity.
transcript.zh: 许多科学家认为，地球如今已经进入第六次大灭绝时期，人类造成的栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化的有害结合，已经导致自1500年以来至少77种哺乳动物和140种鸟类灭绝。这是自6600万年前恐龙灭绝以来最大规模的物种损失。科学家表示，对每一个物种进行测序将彻底改变人们对生物学和进化的认识，加强保护以及维护和恢复生物多样性的努力。

transcript.text: Dr. Tim Littlewood, head of Life Sciences Department at the Natural History Museum, said, "Whether you are interested in food or disease, the history of how every organism on the planet has adapted to its environment is recorded in its genetic makeup. How you then harness that is dependent on your ability to understand it. We will be using modern methods to get a really good window on the present and the past. And of course, a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future."
transcript.zh: 自然历史博物馆生命科学部负责人蒂姆·利特尔伍德博士说：“无论你对食物还是疾病感兴趣，地球上每一种生物如何适应其环境的历史，都记录在它的遗传构成中。你如何利用这些信息，取决于你理解它的能力。我们将运用现代方法，真正清晰地了解现在和过去。当然，了解过去也能为未来提供一个预测模型。”

transcript.text: Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project. Since 1970, humanity has wiped out 60 percent of animal populations. About 23,000 of 80,000 species surveyed are approaching extinction. We are in the midst of the sixth great extinction event of life on our planet, which not only threatens wildlife species, but also imperils the global food supply. As scientists, we all realise we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now. I think we're making history."
transcript.zh: Wellcome科学部主任吉姆·史密斯爵士说：“尽管我努力思考，也想不出还有哪个项目比这更加令人兴奋、更加贴近现实、更加及时，或更能激发国际社会的灵感。自1970年以来，人类已经使动物种群数量减少了60%。在接受调查的8万种物种中，约有2.3万种正走向灭绝。我们正处于地球生命第六次大灭绝事件之中，这不仅威胁野生动物物种，也危及全球粮食供应。作为科学家，我们都意识到，现在迫切需要为我们这个脆弱星球上的生命编制目录。我认为，我们正在创造历史。”

transcript.text: John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century, "No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main." Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise. In his new book, The Self Delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as "self", and not even our bodies are truly "us".
transcript.zh: 英国诗人约翰·多恩在17世纪写道：“没有人是一座孤岛，自成一体；每个人都是大陆的一部分，是陆地的一部分。”如今，一位英国学者声称，人的个体性确实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、身体和文化层面的相互联系，远比人们意识到的更加紧密。在他的新书《The Self Delusion》中，雷丁大学生态学与进化研究组的研究员汤姆·奥利弗教授认为，根本不存在所谓的“自我”，甚至连我们的身体也并不真正是“我们”。

transcript.text: Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity. "A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the centre of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution," he writes. "However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe. You may feel as if you are an independent individual, acting autonomously in the world; that you have an unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor-point with the world changing around you. This is the illusion I seek to tackle. We are intimately connected to the world around us."
transcript.zh: 正如哥白尼意识到地球并不是宇宙的中心一样，奥利弗教授说，社会迫切需要一场类似哥白尼革命的变革，以理解人并非彼此孤立的存在，而是同一个相互联系的身份的一部分。他写道：“人类心智文化演化中的一个重要里程碑，是人们接受地球并不是宇宙的中心，这就是所谓的哥白尼革命。然而，我们还需要摒弃另一个重大的神话：我们以独立自我的身份存在于主观宇宙的中心。你可能会觉得自己是一个独立的个体，在世界上自主行动；觉得自己拥有一个终生持续不变的内在自我，作为一个中心锚点，而世界则在你周围不断变化。这正是我试图应对的幻觉。我们与周围的世界有着密切的联系。”

transcript.text: Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing. In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than 10 years. "Since our bodies are essentially made anew every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient to explain the persistent thread of an identity."
transcript.zh: 奥利弗教授认为，人体内大约有37万亿个细胞，但其中大多数的寿命只有几天或几周，因此构成“我们”的物质一直在变化。事实上，你身体的任何部分都没有存在超过10年。“由于我们的身体本质上每隔几周就会重新形成，仅凭其中的物质显然不足以解释身份持续存在的脉络。”

transcript.text: Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realising we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems. Through selfish over-consumption we are destroying the natural world and using non-renewable resources at an accelerating rate. "We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behaviour to act in less selfish ways," he said. "So let's open our eyes to the hidden connections all around us."
transcript.zh: 奥利弗教授声称，个人主义实际上不利于社会，只有意识到我们是更大实体的一部分，才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题。我们通过自私的过度消费正在摧毁自然世界，并以越来越快的速度消耗不可再生资源。他说：“作为一个物种，我们正处于关键的十字路口，必须迅速改变我们的思维方式和行为，以更加不自私的方式行事。因此，让我们睁开双眼，看清周围隐藏的各种联系。”

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Phyllis Hartman knows what it's like to make one's way through the depths of office meeting hell. Managers at one of her former human resources jobs arranged so many meetings that attendees would fall asleep at the table or intentionally arrive late. With hours of her day blocked up with unnecessary meetings, she was often forced to make up her work during overtime. "I was actually working more hours than I probably would have needed to get the work done," says Hartman, who is founder and president of PGHR Consulting in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: She isn't alone in her frustration. Between 11 million and 55 million meetings are held each day in the United States, costing most organisations between 7% and 15% of their personnel budgets. Every week, employees spend about six hours in meetings, while the average manager meets for a staggering 23 hours.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: And though experts agree that traditional meetings are essential for making certain decisions and developing strategy, some employees view them as one of the most unnecessary parts of the workday. The result is not only hundreds of billions of wasted dollars, but an annoyance of what organisational psychologists call "meeting recovery syndrome (MRS)": time spent cooling off and regaining focus after a useless meeting. If you run to the office kitchen to get some relief with colleagues after a frustrating meeting, you're likely experiencing meeting recovery syndrome.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Meeting recovery syndrome is a concept that should be familiar to almost anyone who has held a formal job. It isn't ground-breaking to say workers feel fatigued after a meeting, but only in recent decades have scientists deemed the condition worthy of further investigation. With its links to organisational efficiency and employee wellbeing, MRS has attracted the attention of psychologists aware of the need to understand its precise causes and cures.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Today, in so far as researchers can hypothesise, MRS is most easily understood as a slow renewal of finite mental and physical resources. When an employee sits through an ineffective meeting their brain power is essentially being drained away. Meetings drain vitality if they last too long, fail to engage employees or turn into one-sided lectures. The conservation of resources theory, originally proposed in 1989 by Dr Stevan Hobfoll, states that psychological stress occurs when a person's resources are threatened or lost. When resources are low, a person will shift into defence to conserve their remaining supply. In the case of office meetings, where some of employees' most valuable resources are their focus, alertness and motivation, this can mean an abrupt halt in productivity as they take time to recover.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: As humans, when we transition from one task to another on the job—say from sitting in a meeting to doing normal work—it takes an effortful cognitive switch. We must detach ourselves from the previous task and expend significant mental energy to move on. If we are already drained to dangerous levels, then making the mental switch to the next thing is extra tough. It's common to see people cyber-loafing after a frustrating meeting, going and getting coffee, interrupting a colleague and telling them about the meeting, and so on.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Each person's ability to recover from horrible meetings is different. Some can bounce back quickly, while others carry their fatigue until the end of the workday. Yet while no formal MRS studies are currently underway, one can loosely speculate on the length of an average employee's lag time. Switching tasks in a non-MRS condition takes about 10 to 15 minutes. With MRS, it may take as long as 45 minutes on average. It's even worse when a worker has several meetings that are separated by 30 minutes. "Not enough time to transition in a non-MRS situation to get anything done, and in an MRS situation, not quite enough time to recover for the next meeting," says researcher Joseph Allen. "Then, add the compounding of back-to-back bad meetings and we may have an epidemic on our hands."

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: In an effort to combat the side effects of MRS, Allen, along with researcher Joseph Mroz and colleagues at the University of Nebraska-Omaha, published a study detailing the best ways to avoid common traps, including a concise checklist of do's and don'ts applicable to any workplace. Drawing from around 200 papers to compile their comprehensive list, Mroz and his team may now hold a remedy to the largely undefined problem of MRS.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Mroz says a good place to start is asking ourselves if our meetings are even necessary in the first place. If all that's on the agenda is a quick catch-up, or some non-urgent information sharing, it may better suit the group to send around an email instead. "The second thing I would always recommend is keep the meeting as small as possible," says Mroz. "If they don't actually have some kind of immediate input, then they can follow up later. They don't need to be sitting in this hour-long meeting." Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to more employee engagement in the meetings they do attend, which experts agree is a proven remedy for MRS.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Employees also feel taxed when they are invited together to meetings that don't inspire participation, says Cliff Scott, professor of organisational science. It takes precious time for them to vent their emotions, complain and try to regain focus after a pointless meeting—one of the main traps of MRS. Over time as employees find themselves tied up in more and more unnecessary meetings—and thus dealing with increasing lag times from MRS—the waste of workday hours can feel insulting.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Despite the relative scarcity of research behind the subject, Hartman has taught herself many of the same tricks suggested in Mroz's study, and has come a long way since her days of being stuck with unnecessary meetings. The people she invites to meetings today include not just the essential employees, but also representatives from every department that might have a stake in the issue at hand. Managers like her, who seek input even from non-experts to shape their decisions, can find greater support and cooperation from their workforce, she says.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: If an organisation were to apply all 22 suggestions from Mroz and Allen's findings, the most noticeable difference would be a stark decrease in the total number of meetings on the schedule, Mroz says. Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to increased productivity, which is the ultimate objective of convening a meeting. While none of the counter-MRS ideas have been tested empirically yet, Allen says one trick with promise is for employees to identify things that quickly change their mood from negative to positive. As simple as it sounds, finding a personal happy place, going there and then coming straight back to work might be key to facilitating recovery.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Leaders should also see themselves as "stewards of everyone else's valuable time", adds Steven Rogelberg, author of The Surprising Science of Meetings. Having the skills to foresee potential traps and treat employees' endurance with care allows leaders to provide effective short-term deterrents to MRS.

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: Most important, however, is for organisations to awaken to the concept of meetings being flexible, says Allen. By reshaping the way they prioritise employees' time, companies can eliminate the very sources of MRS in their tracks.

But a big or steady serving of sarcasm will overwhelm the emotional flavor of any conversation and can taste very bitter to its recipient.

paragraphs.label: H

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities. Sarcastic statements are expressed in a cutting manner; witty remarks are delivered with undisguised and harmless humor.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Variability is crucially important for learning new skills. Consider learning how to serve in tennis. Should you always practise serving from the exactly same location on the court, aiming at the same spot? Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end. This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories. For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: "There are over ten different names for this basic principle," says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study. "Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli."

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling. "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not. But according to the 'Mr. Miyagi principle', practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: But why does variability impact learning and generalisation? One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations. This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical(非典型的) examples.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: "Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life. Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives," explains Raviv. "For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community. Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv. "Our paper raises a lot of open questions. Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?"
